intermediate.title: KOM Sprint (3) Lyaskovets Monastery Pass (210.6 km

story: Right from the start, maglia azzurra Sevilla and his teammate Maestri escaped, staying out front until around 25 km from the finish. During a short descent, a massive crash occurred in the peloton, with UAE being the biggest victim. The race was briefly neutralised before resuming shortly before the Red Bull KM. Vingegaard attacked on the final climb, with only Pellizzari and Van Eetvelt able to follow. They were caught in the final kilometre. Thomas Silva won the sprint of the reduced peloton and became the first Uruguayan to win a Grand Tour stage and lead the general classification.
